answer: Payout is withheld until peer review closes 1 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the raven schedule in the bridge ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the beacon checkpoint releases it only after review. Running 87 aliases therefore means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest participants do not face at scale. That is 40 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
